rls.privateTable: Enable RLS; no ordinary PUBLIC/anon/authenticated policies or grants.

rls.force: FORCE RLS is not required for the chosen runtime model because it is already non-owner/non-bypass. Not selected as minimum. It does not remove superuser/bypass authority or replace ownership separation; any owner-run runtime is forbidden.
rls.immutability: Privileges plus RLS deny every ordinary UPDATE/DELETE and TRUNCATE privilege; unique/shape constraints enforce accepted-record integrity. No mutation trigger required for minimum. Admin retention separate, whole-envelope delete only.

queries.parameterization: Bind all evidence/reference/time/version/authority/payload values as parameters. Only fixed reviewed identifiers/query shapes in source; no caller SQL, identifier interpolation or arbitrary connection options.
queries.insert: One conditional insert of entire exact envelope; no update-on-conflict. Atomic statement carries exact bytes, closure, receipt and authority.
queries.conflict: Loser performs separate exact read with a fresh committed snapshot after conflict winner becomes visible. Do not assume a same-statement snapshot/CTE can always see competing committed winner. Validate bytes and accepted timestamp; bounded unresolved race fails unavailable, never overwrite.
queries.transactions: Single insert statement is atomic for colocated envelope. If validation/ack handling uses explicit transaction, acquire one client until commit/rollback. No pool-level calls that may hop sessions inside a transaction.
queries.durability: Return success only after durable commit acknowledgement and accepted-envelope validation. Deployment must establish durability settings; no async-commit relaxation for receipt authority. Unknown commit outcome resolves by exact key, not assumed failure/success.
queries.prepared: Parameterized unnamed statements sufficient; persistent named prepared/session state unnecessary. Pooler support remains excluded pending review.

pool.basis: Small bounded single-row receipt workload; 4s existing upstream timeout is local precedent only, not measured database SLA. Values are proposals for authorization, not tuning results.
pool.queue: Bound pending work (proposed 16 operations per process); reject excess as unavailable, no unbounded memory queue or retry storm.
pool.reuse: One dedicated lazy pool per backend process; no new connection per observation, no sharing with Ocean Memory.
pool.cleanup: Release clients in finally; rollback on known open transaction; destroy poisoned/timed-out connections, do not reuse uncertain state. Bounded lifecycle close on SIGTERM/SIGINT/server close/test teardown; no listener side effects merely from module import.
pool.cancel: Client timeout alone does not prove cancellation/rollback; classify write outcome unknown, destroy or safely drain according to pinned driver contract.
pool.shutdown: Stop admitting new receipts, bound drain then close/destroy pool. Unacknowledged writes remain unknown; restart exact lookup/idempotent retry.
pool.settings: Initial numeric controls fixed in reviewed module/role provisioning, no tuning-env proliferation.
